newsitem.title: FINLAND: New routes to Russia via Helsinki Gateway terminal.
newsitem.headline: New routes to Russia via Helsinki Gateway terminal.

text.p: A new passenger terminal at Helsinki airport will facilitate transit to exotic destinations in Russia, Martti Suomela, marketing head of an international tourism and travel fair here, said on Tuesday.

The two-day fair, the Helsinki Gateway Convention, was to coincide with the official opening of the Helsinki Gateway Terminal -- a new building connecting the Helsinki airport's domestic and international passenger terminals.
"Fishing expeditions to the Kola peninsula (in Russia) are a special (travel) package planned as a gateway-product," Suomela said in a statement.

Sport anglers eager to try new waters can take Finnair's Saturday flight to Murmansk from Helsinki, and the package includes a connecting two-hour helicopter flight "to the best salmon rivers in Eastern Murmansk", he said.
Tailor-made packages are also on offer, Suomela said.
"There are 400-500 destinations in Russia without any scheduled flight connections, but to which small jets can fly," he said. "Jets are used by oil experts working on Russian oil fields," he said.

The Helsinki airport's gateway or transit traffic had increased about 18 percent per year in the past three years, Suomela said. This year, some 300,000 people will stay at Helsinki airport for stop-overs of a couple of hours, he said.
